vocabulary.definition: European Union (EU): originally created after World War Two to help bring peace, stability and economic prosperity to Europe. It was believed that another major European war could be avoided by increasing economic cooperation between European countries.

a racist political system that existed in South Africa from 1948 until the early 1990s. A system of official laws that seperated persons along skin colour lines and gave privileges to persons of white European ancestry only.

an international forum for addressing many of the common concerns and challenges of the arctic states and indigenous communities. Members include Canada, Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, Russian Federation, Sweden, and the United States.
economic trade or diplomatic relations between two countries
to refuse to deal with (an organization or country) as a protest against its actions or policies
located or found in one of the polar regions (North or South Pole)
a period of tensions short of actual war between the ideologically opposed USA and Soviet Union from 1946 - 1991.

a military alliance of countries that agree to come to the defence of a member country if attacked by a country outside the alliance. For example, NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organization) nations originally joined together to provide protection from attack by the former Soviet Union. The alliances before World War I are another example of collective defence.
the safety (security) of the group (collective)
former colonies of the British Empire who grouped together for their common interests
when two or more sides are in opposition to eachother
the process of countries speaking to one another to make agreements peacefully with each other.
a list of new terms that you will encounter in this unit. Click on each one for a definition:
help provided to nations in need
the methods a country uses while dealing with other countries
the theoretical situation where there are no restrictions on trade between nations - no tariffs, duties, subsidies or other barriers to trade.

the Group of Eight is a group of eight nations with highly developed economies. Originally a forum for dealing with economic issues, it now has a broader agenda including international economic, political and social issues.
Gross Domestic Product - a measure of a country's national income. Also Gross Dometic Income (GDI)..
an understanding or awareness of global affairs and human conditions in various regions around the world
occurs when the Earth's atmosphere experiences an increase in average temperatures.
the process by which people around the world are becoming increasingly interconnected through trade, the media, and migration
the belief that human conditions can be made better for people
a theory or concept about the way in which society should be organized
(or colonialism) the purpose or process of a dominant country extending its control over another, weaker country or territory
literally, "between nations." Anything between nations. Usually used in reference to nation states rather than other definitions of "nation".

Rules and regulations governing the conduct between nations. The need for international laws was understood many years ago by the United Nations. The United Nations has therefore become the primary maker of international law. A UN sponsored World Court helps to interpret those laws whenever disputes between nations arises. So, a nation can take a dispute regarding international law to the World Court. For example, back in 1958, the Law of the Sea was created governing a nation's territorial limits along its ocean shoreline and also pollution at sea. Countries could then bring disputes about their territorial limits to the World Court.

The doctrine that all members of the global community accept collective responsibility for the challenges that face the world and that the motives of nations and nation-states must be respected in the search for solutions. Some may see it as placing global concerns before a country's own national interests, or the best way to protect national interests.
the foreign policy of intervening in the affairs of another country
a policy of non-involvement in international affairs
isolationism: a policy of non-involvement in international affairs
an organization of over 50 nations that promotes peaceful cooperation between french speaking communities.
the reason or cause that moves a person to act in a particular way.
the policy of pursueing agreements, discussions or negotiations between multiple countries (3 or more).
orth America Free Trade Agreement - a trade agreement signed in 1995 by Canada, USA, and Mexico.
the policy of not taking sides or entering into alliances.

Non-governmental organization- This term refers to organizations that are not for profit and independent of the government. Many Canadian NGOs carry out projects to help people in developing countries meet their basic needs, but they also raise awareness in Canada about development issues and raise funds for projects.
the foreign policy of not getting involved in the affairs of other countries
a water route between the Atlantic Ocean and the Pacific Ocean along the northern coast of North America; mostly through the Canadian North

aims to end an active conflict between two parties by using the armed forces of a third country, or coalition of countries, to impose peace. Peace enforcement troops would be more heavily armed than peacekeepers. Unlike peacekeeping, permission from the host country is not necessary in peace-enforcement, especially if human rights or civilians are at risk. Peace-enforcement troops can conduct offensive operations.
immediately after an armed conflict has ended, soldiers from other countries are placed between the aggressive groups to observe and maintain the peace process.

A policy of preventing armed conflict through diplomacy. While peacekeeping aims to keep opposing sides away from each other after an armed conflict, "peacemaking" aims to prevent armed conflict through diplomacy. Peacemaking diplomacy is also used after an armed conflict has been stopped in order to negotiate a permanent peace agreement.
the point of view that is shaped by one's background and experiences

Putting tariffs (taxes) on imported goods to make them more expensive so that your own goods will seem cheaper and sell better. As well, quotas may be created to limit how much of an import comes into your country. This will also help to keep import prices high, which will protect goods made in your country. It’s all done to make people want to buy goods made in their own country which is intended to protect local industries and jobs.
when a country seeks to be safe (secure) from military or even economic aggression by other countries
the freedom of a nation to make its own decisions independent of outside influences from other countries; similar to sovereignty
a country that is free from control by any other country
Sovereignty is the authority of a state to govern itself and make its own decisions.
The extent to which a nation is able to extend its influence beyond its borders.
individuals or groups that can be affected by the actions of an organization.
the foreign policy of getting involved in the affairs of other countries
the foreign policy of not getting involved in the affairs of other countries
a form of internationalism in which nations agree to abide by the decisions of an international organization.
economic, cultural and social development that preserves resources and the environment so that they will be able to continue indefinately.
taxes placed by a government on imported or exported goods and services.
is foreign assistance (money) given by one country to a second country on condition the money is spent in the country giving the aid.
Working across national borders. Transnationals do not involve governments, though they sometimes work with governments.
Acting alone without international approval or agreements.
an international organization whose aims are to foster global cooperation in international law, international peace and security, economic development, social progress and human rights issues.
an organization dedicated to the worldwide protection of aboriginal rights.
is the concept of a global political body that would make, interpret and enforce international law
a multilateral organization dedicated to reducing trade barriers and establishing and enforcing the rules of international trade.
